abstract: We compared chest computerized tomography (CT) to chest x-ray as chest staging modalities in testis cancer patients on the basis of abdominal CT findings. We identified 92 patients who presented with negative staging abdominal CT scans and 52 with abnormal abdominal CT scans. Of these patients 42 and 32, respectively, underwent a chest x-ray and chest CT concurrently as part of the initial staging evaluation. Dictated x-ray reports were used to compare study findings. Findings on chest x-ray and chest CT were considered concordant if both studies identified similar chest abnormalities. Findings were considered discordant if either study failed to identify an abnormality noted on the other test. Patient outcome during followup, response to therapy or chest pathology was used to discriminate benign from malignant radiological abnormalities. Radiographic chest abnormalities (chest x-ray and/or chest CT) were identified in 12 of the 42 patients with negative abdominal CT scans. Three of these 12 studies represented metastasis with the remainder being benign. Imaging results were concordant in all 3 patients with chest metastasis and 5 of 9 with benign chest disease. Chest x-ray identified abnormalities not observed on chest CT in 1 patient, with chest CT identifying abnormalities not observed on chest x-ray in 3. Radiographic chest abnormalities (chest x-ray and/or chest CT) were identified in 15 of 32 patients who had a positive abdominal CT. All chest lesions identified in these patients were believed to represent metastatic disease. Chest x-ray failed to identify abnormalities present on chest CT in 4 of the 15 patients. The use of chest CT as a staging modality in abdominal CT negative patients failed to increase diagnostic sensitivity relative to chest x-ray alone. However, in 32 patients with abnormal abdominal CT scans the use of chest x-ray alone would have missed intrathoracic metastatic disease in 4. These data suggest that chest x-ray may be the preferred initial chest staging study for testis cancer patients with negative abdominal CT, while chest CT is mandated in patients with abnormal abdominal CT.
abstract_ja: われわれは、腹部CTの結果に基づき、精巣がん患者の胸部病期分類の画像モダリティとして胸部CTと胸部X線を比較した。腹部病期分類CTが陰性の92例と異常の52例を同定した。このうち、それぞれ42例と32例で胸部X線と胸部CTを同時に病期分類の初回評価の一環として施行した。胸部X線と胸部CTの所見は、両検査が類似した胸部異常を同定した場合に一致（concordant）とした。いずれかの検査が他方で認められた異常を同定できなかった場合は不一致（discordant）とした。良性と悪性の放射線学的異常の識別には、経過観察中の患者転帰、治療への反応、または胸部病理所見を用いた。腹部CT陰性の42例中12例で胸部の放射線学的異常（胸部X線および/または胸部CT）が認められた。この12例のうち3例は転移で、残りは良性であった。胸部転移を有する3例では全例で所見が一致し、良性胸部疾患を有する9例中5例でも一致した。胸部X線では胸部CTで認められない異常が1例、胸部CTではX線で認められない異常が3例に認められた。腹部CTが陽性の32例中15例で胸部の放射線学的異常（胸部X線および/または胸部CT）が認められた。これらの患者で同定された胸部病変は、いずれも転移性疾患と考えられた。胸部X線は、15例中4例で胸部CTに認められた異常を同定できなかった。腹部CT陰性患者において病期分類の検査として胸部CTを用いても、胸部X線単独に比べて診断感度は向上しなかった。しかし、腹部CT異常のある32例では、胸部X線のみでは4例で胸腔内転移性疾患を見逃していた可能性があった。これらのデータは、腹部CT陰性の精巣がん患者では胸部X線が初回の胸部病期分類検査として望ましく、腹部CT異常の患者では胸部CTが必要であることを示唆する。
